subject: Architecture
title: Responsive Facades: Buildings That Adapt
description: A short lesson to help you apply Responsive Facades: Buildings That Adapt.

hook.text: What if building walls could open and close like skin pores — adapting to sun, wind, and rain automatically?

buildup.text: Responsive facades use sensors and motors to adjust shading panels, louvers, and vents throughout the day.

discovery.text: The Al Bahar Towers in Abu Dhabi have 2,000 umbrella-like panels that open and close to block desert sun.

twist.text: These mashrabiya-inspired screens reduce solar gain by 50% — cutting air conditioning costs dramatically.

climax.text: New materials can change opacity without motors — electrochromic glass darkens with an electric current.

punchline.text: Buildings that breathe. Walls that think. Architecture is coming alive.

quiz.question: How do the Al Bahar Towers reduce solar heat gain?
options: Reflective mirrors bounce sunlight away from the building
2,000 umbrella-like panels open and close to block the sun
Underground cooling pipes circulate cold water through walls
